citations.desc: Primary enclosures used to transport live birds.
citations.narrative:
The transport enclosure for the Great Horned Owl does not have the projecting rims or other devices to prevent
obstruction of the ventilation openings. The projecting rims or similar devices must be large enough to provide a minimum
air circulation space of 0.75 inches between the primary enclosure and anything the enclosure is adjacent to, unless 90
percent or greater of the surface area of the enclosure wall is open (e.g., cage mesh). Adequate space for air circulation
and ventilation during transport ensures the welfare of the birds transported.
Correct by 13 July, 2026
This is a 1st Re-License Inspection for a Class “C” license. The inspection and exit briefing were conducted with the
applicant.
All items must be in compliance within 2 more inspections or by 8 September, 2026 or the applicant will forfeit the license
fee and must wait 6 months to reapply. Please contact your inspector to schedule your next Re-License Inspection.
Regulated activity may continue at all regulated sites until expiration of the current license on 19 July 2026. At that time,
conducting regulated activity from any site without a valid USDA license is a violation of the Animal Welfare Act.
